findings.location: OrganisationStructureMigrator.cs:36-45 and :67-76; acceptance.md failure B1 'Migrator self-check fails' and 'Another instance committed first'
findings.obligation: Design names two failure points of the start-up step (self-check failure rolls back and stops the start; losing instance re-reads the winner's structure); code-craftsmanship rule 30: a test observes each named failure point or the closing statement says why it is unreachable
findings.observation: No test in TwoLevelsFromTerminologyTest or MappingFromUnitsTest drives either path. Quote: 'catch (DbUpdateException exception)' ... 'logger.LogInformation(exception, "Another instance built the organisation structure first; using its levels and mappings");' and 'throw new InvalidOperationException("The upgrade to levels stopped and changed nothing: its check that every unit keeps all its item types failed for "'. Both branches pass with every run green; a mutant removing the catch or the check survives. Not blocking for S2: the happy path and idempotent second start are observed on SQLite and Postgres (14 passed).
findings.remediation: Acceptance designer adds (a) a case where a second Seed runs after the first committed between the Load and the insert (e.g. pre-insert the structure row via a second context, then Seed) and asserts the first structure and mappings are kept and no exception; (b) a case whose self-check cannot pass (a unit with a type no mapping lists) asserting the tables stay empty and the refusal text names the unit. Or state in the record why unreachable.

findings.obligation: nw-code-craftsmanship rule 21 (never a silent wrong success) and ports-and-adapters wiring: a dependency whose absence changes behaviour must not be optional
findings.observation: Quote: 'public class TerminologyService(IRepository<TerminologyEntry> repository, IOrganisationStructureStore? structureStore = null) : ITerminologyService'. The module registers the service in AddOrganisationSetup (OrganisationSetupModule.cs:24) and the store only in AddOrganisationStructure (:34), so a composition that calls the first without the second silently reads and writes only the old rows, and the levels then drift from the words with no error. Program.cs registers both today, so no user-visible defect in the shipped host. Same line :62 'structureStore?.Load(CancellationToken.None).GetAwaiter().GetResult()' is sync-over-async on the request thread; safe without a synchronization context, blocks a pool thread; acceptable given the synchronous port, but it is the reason to keep the port change on the list for slice 04+.
findings.remediation: Make the store a required constructor parameter and register it where the service is registered (or register both in one extension); update the test compositions that omit it. Non-blocking for S2.

findings.location: TerminologyService.cs:9-10 (doc: 'Their old rows are still written, so a previous release rolled back to shows the same words') and TerminologyService.cs:72
findings.obligation: Rows and levels cannot drift: one source of truth for the eight words after rollback and roll-forward
findings.observation: Quote: 'Value = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(entry.Value) ? entry.Value : words?.WordFor(entry.Key) ?? entry.Value'. After a rollback the previous release renames Team to Crew in the rows only; on the next upgrade the structure exists, so the migrator does not run and GetAll answers the stale level word, discarding the rename. The architecture's rollback detection covers only WorkItemTypes, not the eight words. Also OwnerTerms.From (Domain/OwnerTerms.cs:14) still reads the eight rows directly, a second reader of the same words. No drift inside one release (every write in UpdateTerminology goes to both), so not blocking for S2.
findings.remediation: Design decides: either re-derive the level names from the rows on start when the rows differ from the levels and the rows were edited after the upgrade, or document that a rename made on a rolled-back release is lost; and route OwnerTerms through the levels in a later slice.

findings.obligation: sc-review Dimension 1: no feature without an accepted outcome that reads it; command-query separation
findings.observation: Quote: 'Task<ConnectionMapping> ForConnection(int connectionId, CancellationToken cancellationToken);' with doc 'or a new one with the create defaults, saved with the caller's unit of work'. No production or test caller exists in this slice (grep over Lighthouse.Backend and Tests finds only the declaration and implementation), and it stages an insert into the change tracker from a read method. Not blocking: slice 04 is its stated consumer.
findings.remediation: Remove it from this slice and add it with its first consumer in slice 04, or keep it and let slice 04's oracle observe it; make the staging explicit (separate Create method) when it is used.

findings.obligation: Seeders share one scoped context; a step must not discard another step's pending state
findings.observation: Quote: 'context.ChangeTracker.Clear();' as the first statement of TheFirstUpgrade. Every seeder before it (TerminologySeeder.cs saves at its end) saves, so nothing is lost today, but a seeder registered earlier that stages without saving would lose its changes silently. Low risk; also the catch at :38 clears again.
findings.remediation: Scope the clear to the entities the upgrade tracks, or assert no pending changes (context.ChangeTracker.HasChanges()) and refuse loudly. Non-blocking.

findings.obligation: Architectural test checks the law over everything it governs, never a fixed file list (nw-code-design-oo section 7)
findings.observation: Quote: 'private static readonly string[] ThePlanner = [typeof(OrganisationStructureMigrationPlan).FullName!, typeof(PlannedLevel).FullName!, typeof(PlannedMapping).FullName!];'. Only the three named types are checked and only direct IL references; a Domain type the planner calls (ConnectionMapping, OrganisationStructure) that later reaches storage would pass. The negative control (The_rule_catches_a_type_that_reaches_storage) is good. Non-blocking.
findings.remediation: Also assert the Domain.Structure and Domain.Mapping namespaces have no storage, clock or I/O dependency, so purity is by namespace rather than by list.
